senses.gloss:
वप् वप्, cl. 1. P. A. वपति, वपते,
उवाप (1st sing. उवप or उवाप, 2nd
sing. उवपिथ), ऊपे (according to some also [आ]वेपे),
वप्स्यति, -ते (ep. वपिष्यति), अवाप्सीत्, अवप्त,
वप्तुम्, to shear, cut, shave (the hair, beard, &c.,
Ved.); to shear off, crop off, eat off, graze, mow
(grass &c., in Ṛg-veda VI. 6, 4. वपन्ति = मुण्-
डयन्ति); to shave one's self, be shaven or shorn
(Ved. A.); to strew, scatter (especially seed), sow
[]
seed, sow, plant; to throw, cast (dice &c.); to pro-
create, beget; to weave, (in this sense probably a
kind of Caus. of rt. वे): Pass. उप्यते (Part. उप्त,
q. v.; the forms उपित and वपित are also given),
to be scattered or sown: Caus. वापयति, -यते,
-यितुम्, Aor. अवीवपत्, to cause to shear or shave
(Ved.); to cause to be shorn (Ved. A.); to sow,
put in the ground, plant: Desid. विवप्सति, -ते:
Intens. वावप्यते, वावप्ति; [cf. Gr. ὀπυίω, οἴφω,
οἰφέω, (perhaps also) ὅπλοω, ὑφαίνω; Angl. Sax.
wif, wœpen; Goth. vepn.]

वप, अस्, m. shaving, shearing; one who sows, a
sower; sowing seed; weaving; (आ), f. the skin or
covering of the intestines, omentum; the mucous or
glutinous secretion of the bones or flesh, marrow, fat
(= मेदस्, q. v.); a mound or heap thrown up by
ants; a cavity, hollow, hole.
—वपा-कृत्, त्, m.
marrow.
—वपा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, furnished with
omentum, enveloped in omentum, covered with fat,
&c.
—वपोदर (˚पा-उद्˚), अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. fat-
bellied, corpulent (said of Indra).
वपा. See under वप above.
वप्प वप्प or वप्पक, अस्, m., N. of a king.

वाप वाप, अस्, m. (fr. rt. वप् or connected
with Caus. of rt. वे), sowing seed; weaving; shear-
ing, shaving.
—वाप-दण्ड, अस्, m. a weaver's
loom; [cf. वाय-दण्ड.]

वपन, अम्, n. the act of shearing, shaving; the
act of sowing seed, sowing; semen virile; (ई), f. a
barber's shop.

वापन, अम्, n. the act of causing to sow or
sowing; shaving, shearing.

वपनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be shorn [cf. केश-व्˚];
to be sown.
वपिल, अस्, m. a procreator, father.
वपु, उस्, m. a body; (उस्), f., N. of an Apsaras.

वपुन, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. वप्), a deity;
(अम्), n. knowledge, (probably for वयुन.)
वपुर्-धर. See under वपुस् below.

वपुष, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. = वपुस्, having form
or beautiful form, handsome, (according to modern
Vedic scholars also) wonderful; (अम्), n. beauty or
elegance of form, wonderful figure, (Sāy. on Ṛg-veda
III. 2, 15. वपुषाय = रूपार्थम्, for beauty of
form, on account of beauty of form); body, form,
(at the end of a comp., cf. वराह-व्˚); (आ), f. a
particular article of commerce (= हवुषा?).

1. वपुष्य, Nom. P. वपुष्यति, &c., Ved. to
cause beauty or lustre of form, (Sāy. वपुर्-दीप्तिं
कृ); to desire form or beauty of form, (Sāy. =
वपुर् इष्); to wonder, be astonished, (this latter
sense is thought probable by modern scholars.)

2. वपुष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having form or
beauty of form, handsome; conducive to bodily
welfare, (Sāy. = वपुषि हित); wonderfully beauti-
ful, wonderful.

वपुस्, उस्, उस्, उस्, having form or beautiful form
(Ved.), embodied, handsome, (according to modern
Vedic scholars also) wonderful; (उस्), n. form, figure,
shape, body, person, appearance; essence, nature,
character; a beautiful form or figure; beautiful ap-
pearance, beauty, (वपुषे, dat. c. for beauty of
form, in order to be beautiful); beautiful or won-
derful appearance of any kind, (according to modern
Vedic scholars) marvellous phenomenon, wonder;
water (according to Naigh. I. 12); N. of a daughter
of Dakṣa and wife of Dharma.
—वपुः-प्रकर्-
ष, अस्, m. excellence of form, personal beauty.
—वपुः-स्रव, अस्, m. a humor of the body.
—वपुर्-धर, अस्, आ, अम्, having form, em-
bodied, having beautiful form, beautiful, handsome.
—वपुष्-टम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. most beautiful
or excellent in form, most beautiful or handsome;
most wonderful; (आ), f. Hibiscus Mutabilis; N.
of the wife of Janam-ejaya.
—वपुष्-टर, अस्,
आ, अम्, Ved. more or most beautiful in form,
more handsome, more or most wonderful.
—व-
पुष्-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a body, corpo-
real, corporate, embodied; having a beautiful form,
beautiful, handsome; containing the word वपुस्;
(आन्), m., N. of a deity enumerated among the
Viśve Devāḥ; of a son of Priya-vrata; of a king
of Kuṇḍina; (अती), f., N. of one of the Mātṛs
attending upon Skanda.
—वपुष्-मत, अस्, m.,
N. of a king of Kuṇḍina, (for वपुष्-मत्.)
—वपुस्-सात्, ind. into the state of a body, to a
form or body.

वप्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be sown; to be immitted
[]
seminally; to be impregnated or begotten; to be
implanted, to be given or conferred.

वप्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who shears, a shearer,
cutter, shaver; one who sows or plants, a planter,
sower, husbandman; (ता), m. one who fertilizes or
fecundates, a procreator, progenitor, father; a poet,
sage.
वप्य-नील, N. of a country.

वप्र, अस्, अम्, m. n. a rampart, earth-work,
mud-wall, mound, hillock, earth taken from the
ditch of a town and raised as a wall or buttress;
the foundation of a building; the gate of a fortified
city; the bank of a river, shore or bank in general,
(अनु-वप्रम्, along the bank or shore, Kirāt. VI.
4); the slope or declivity of a hill, table-land on a
mountain; a ditch; the circumference of a sphere or
globe; a sown field, field in general; dust, earth;
the butting of an elephant or bull, (see वप्र-
क्रीडा); = निष्-कुट, वन-ज, वाजिका (?), पाटीर;
(अम्), n. lead [cf. वर्ध्र]; (अस्), m. a father
[cf. वप्तृ]; = प्रजा-पति; N. of a Vyāsa in the
fourteenth division of the Dvāpara age; of a son of
the fourteenth Manu; (आ), f. Bengal madder (=
मञ्जिष्ठा); N. of the mother of Nimi (the
twenty-first Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī); (ई),
f. a hillock, ant-hill.
—वप्र-क्रिया, f. = वप्र-
क्रीडा below.
—वप्र-क्रीडा, f. the playful butting
(of an elephant or bull) against a bank or mound of
any kind, (this is called तटाघात in Kumāra-s. II.
50.)
—वप्रानत (˚र-आन्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, bowed or
stooping to butt at a bank or wall.
—वप्रान्तर्
(˚र-अन्˚), ind. in or between banks or mounds.
—वप्राभिघात (˚र-अभ्˚), अस्, m. butting at a
bank or mound.
—वप्राम्भः-स्रुति, इस्, f. the
stream of water flowing along a bank or issuing
from a bank, a rivulet.
—वप्राम्भस् (˚र-अम्˚),
अस्, n. the water flowing along a bank.
वप्रक, अस्, m. the circumference of a sphere.
वप्रि = क्षेत्र, a field; = दुर्-गति, समुद्र.

वप्सस्, Ved. form, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-
veda I. 181, 8 = वपुस् or रूप.)

वपाटिका व-पाटिका, f. = अव-पाटिका, lacera-
tion of the prepuce.

वप्पट-देवी, f., N. of a princess, (also read
वप्यट-देवी.)
वप्पीय or वप्पीयक, अस्, m., N. of a king.

वप्पीह वप्पीह, अस्, m. Cuculus Melano-
leucus (= चातक).

वापक, अस्, आ, अम्, causing to sow (seed &c.);
causing to weave, &c.

वापि, इस्, or वापी, f. (according to Uṇādi-s. IV.
124. fr. rt. वप्), a large oblong pond, an oblong
reservoir of water, a pool or lake; क्रीडा-वापी, f.,
Ved. ‘pleasure-pond,’ a pond in which tortoises,
fishes, &c. are kept for amusement.
—वापी-ह, अस्,
m. ‘abandoning pools,’ the Cātaka bird, Cuculus
Melanoleucos.

वापित, अस्, आ, अम्, caused to be sown, sown (as
seed); shaven, shorn.

वाप्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be sown, to be cast or
thrown; (अस्), m. Costus Speciosus (= कुष्ठ).
वापिका, f. an oblong tank.
